new_task_1.title: Fix importlib mode handling for root-level __init__.py test modules
new_task_1.description: Pytest's importlib-based module naming logic incorrectly stripped the `__init__` segment from a path even when the `__init__.py` file was located at the import root. That produced an empty module name and could break collection or importing when a project root itself contained a `__init__.py` file. The fix only removes the trailing `__init__` segment when it belongs to a package below the root, preserving `__init__` for root-level files.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `module_name_from_path()` does not collapse a root-level `__init__.py` into an empty module name. Previously, when pytest ran with `--import-mode=importlib` and the collection root contained a `__init__.py` file, the module name calculation stripped `__init__` unconditionally, which could prevent correct importing and test execution.

expectation.grounded: When computing a module name from a path relative to the root, pytest must only drop the final `__init__` path part if there is at least one preceding path component. For `root/pkg/__init__.py`, the module name should remain `pkg`. For `root/__init__.py`, the module name should be `__init__`, not an empty string.
expectation.conceptual: Package `__init__.py` files inside subpackages should continue to map to the package name, but a root-level `__init__.py` must still produce a non-empty importable module name so importlib mode can collect and run tests normally.

constraints.grounded: The existing package behavior for nested `__init__.py` files must remain unchanged. Only the special case where the relative path consists solely of `__init__` should change. Other module-name derivation rules based on the relative path to the root must continue to behave the same way.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be narrowly scoped to avoid changing import semantics for ordinary packages. It should preserve prior behavior for modules under subdirectories while correcting the root-package edge case.

behavior: A root-level `__init__.py` now maps to the module name `__init__` instead of being reduced to an empty module name.
Nested package `__init__.py` files continue to omit the trailing `__init__` segment and map to their package path.
Running pytest with `--import-mode=importlib` in a project whose root contains `__init__.py` no longer fails because of invalid module-name generation.
Test collection and execution continue to work for normal package layouts while also supporting the root-package edge case.
acceptance_criteria: Given a path `root/pkg/__init__.py` with `root` as the import root, when pytest computes the module name, then the result should be `pkg`.
Given a path `root/__init__.py` with `root` as the import root, when pytest computes the module name, then the result should be `__init__` rather than an empty string.
Given a test project whose root contains a `__init__.py` file and at least one test file, when pytest runs with `--import-mode=importlib`, then collection and execution should succeed.
Given a project layout without a root-level `__init__.py`, when pytest computes module names, then behavior should remain unchanged from previous versions.
